title: Perkins' character, strict lessons and his lamp-lit back-room studio
summary: Perkins was light-skinned, friendly but strict, demonstrated on each instrument, and taught in a back room by oil lamp.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Learning your horn: teachers, lessons and fees

blocks.x: I understand he was very light colored. He was, he was.
If you didn't know him you'd take him for white man. If you didn't know him.
Was he a friendly sort of fellow?
Was he very strict on his pupils?

Oh yeah, he was strict. If you went there, you see when you take a lesson and, uh, when you get through, you say, well we'll try this next week. He'll turn that page. He'll run two, three lines with you, say that'll be enough for you to practice. And he'll stay on that with you 10 or 15 minutes and give you an idea of it. All right, you go back next week and you don't make one note or don't do nothing with that lesson at all. He'll tell you, you have been practicing, go back home and come back next week. Now let me show you how that goes and he'll show you again.
Did he play it for you?

He played, when he taught you he picked up the trombone right side of you, the trumpet the same way, bass the same way. He had a little upright bass there. Little bit of thing, looked like a, looked almost like an upright alto. It was very small but it had good volume, one of them old timers, you know. And he'd pick that up, each scholar. The drums the same way.
What was the studio like? Was it in the front room or back?

No, it was in the back. It was in the back. It was between his bedroom and the kitchen. And they had like a, like a stairs to go up, upstairs. It had, well it wasn't no upstairs but it was a law. And they had a hole cut in the ceiling. And this thing was made something like a ladder. And he used to go up on that thing and that's where he had all those instruments up there. And all that old music and stuff he had up there.
Did he have a piano in the room?
No, he didn't have no piano, no.
Any music racks much or bench?

Oh yeah, he had plenty of music racks. Had plenty of music racks and chairs, a lot of chairs in there and all. And he used to be, he'd teach in that room. He taught us by oil lamps, no electric. But those lamps were the brightest day. Miss Perkins kept them that way. And he would set that lamp in front of you and put a card behind it to keep it from the light glaring you. And it would shine on the music. And he would always sit on your right and let you be on the left.
That's a very good picture of how they placed the lamp and how you studied it.
